title: A Escarpment for the Provision
premise: Rafael Okonkwo, a railroad engineer who vanished into survey work after a bridge collapse killed her crew, is hired by her old rival Marguerite Voss to reopen the Kestrel Line through the escarpment before winter snows seal the pass. The route crosses land Rafael swore off: the gorge where her brother died and where the deed to their family's stolen provision lands was buried with him. As Voss's crew pushes toward the summit, Rafael discovers the job is a cover for Voss to claim the inheritance papers first, and she must choose between finishing the line that would redeem her name and destroying it to keep justice out of Voss's hands. Racing the snows and the monsoon's early landfall, Rafael reaches the buried cache, burns the fraudulent claim, and lets the line close forever—walking out of the range owning nothing but the truth and, for the first time in three years, her own years instead of miles.
about_author: Juniper Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former field cartographer who spent a decade mapping decommissioned rail corridors across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people who measure their lives in terrain, and she still refuses to fly over mountain ranges.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Three years after the Ashcombe Bridge collapse, Rafael surveys closed rail lines for hire, keeping moving so grief can't catch her. A telegram from Marguerite Voss—her rival and the engineer whose testimony ended her career—offers a fortune for one last job on the Kestrel Line. Emotional beat: restless avoidance cracked open by temptation.

chapters.title: The Sworn-Off Job
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. She refuses, but Voss arrives in person at a dusty junction hotel, revealing the contract includes the Gorge of Provision—the stretch of line where Rafael's brother Tomas died and where their family's land deed supposedly lies buried. Emotional beat: old wounds reopened; pride versus dread.

chapters.title: Crew of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Needing money and answers, Rafael assembles a small crew: aging blaster Okoye, young surveyor Nell, and drifter cook Baptiste, each carrying their own reasons to be invisible. They sign on knowing the season is wrong. Emotional beat: wary fellowship forming among people who trust no one.

chapters.title: Voss's Terms
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Marguerite reveals her own stake: her family financed the original line and lost everything when the provision lands were seized. Her motives seem honorable, but she withholds one document—a court order naming Rafael's late father as the fraud. Emotional beat: sympathy seeded with suspicion.

chapters.title: Into the Foothills
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. The crew enters the foothills ahead of schedule, racing weather reports of an early monsoon. Nell idolizes Rafael and begins noticing how Rafael flinches at every mile marker toward the gorge. Emotional beat: admiration shading into unease.

chapters.title: The First Trestle
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The crew rebuilds a collapsed trestle in record time, proving they can make the pass—but Rafael finds fresh dynamite crates stamped with Voss's company mark, far more than the job requires. Emotional beat: competence and confidence undercut by creeping doubt.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Baptiste's POV. Fishing the gorge river, Baptiste pulls up rusted ironwork from the old disaster and quietly buries it rather than show Rafael. He knows more about the collapse than he's admitted—he worked the rival crew that day. Emotional beat: guilt carried alone.

chapters.title: Snowline Rising
chapters.summary: Okoye's POV. The veteran blaster warns that the high pass will close weeks early this year; they have ten days, not twenty. Voss pushes them faster anyway. Okoye, who has buried friends under avalanches, starts planning his own exit. Emotional beat: professional fear versus loyalty.

chapters.title: The Marker at Mile Forty-One
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. At the mile marker nearest where Tomas died, Rafael finds a cairn someone has maintained for years—fresh flowers, a tin plate. Someone else has been grieving here. Emotional beat: the discovery that she was not the only one who never let go.

chapters.title: Voss's Other Map
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Nell catches Voss comparing two maps: the engineering survey and an older hand-drawn chart marking not track but a burial site in the gorge wall. When confronted, Voss claims it's family history. Emotional beat: the crew's trust fractures.

chapters.title: Storm Front
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The monsoon makes landfall early; rain floods the lower camps while snow seals the upper pass behind them. Retreat is gone. The only way out is through. Emotional beat: commitment forced by circumstance—no way back but forward.

chapters.title: Baptiste Confesses
chapters.summary: Baptiste's POV. Cornered by the storm and his conscience, Baptiste tells Rafael the truth: the Ashcombe Bridge didn't fail by accident. His old crew cut corners on Voss's family's orders, and the report blaming Rafael was bought. Emotional beat: devastating revelation; rage and vertigo.

chapters.title: The Court Order
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael confronts Voss with the confession. Voss admits her father framed Rafael's father to seize the provision lands—and that the deed proving the theft is buried in the gorge with Tomas. Voss wants it to restore her name; Rafael realizes it could also clear hers. Emotional beat: enemies discovering they are mirror images.

chapters.title: Divided Crew
chapters.summary: Okoye's POV. The crew splits: some want to finish the line and get paid; others want to dig for the deed. Okoye forces a vote, and Rafael, torn between redemption and revenge, chooses the line—buying time to plan. Emotional beat: leadership under fracture.

chapters.title: The Gorge Wall
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Working the line through the gorge where Tomas died, Rafael finally grieves properly, telling his story aloud to Nell as they drill the rock face. The work becomes a wake. Emotional beat: catharsis through labor.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Someone destroys a section of completed track overnight. Evidence points to a hired man in Voss's employ—one who isn't there for the line at all, but to ensure the deed is never found by anyone. Emotional beat: paranoia; the enemy was inside all along.

chapters.title: The Man from the Company
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss confronts her father's old fixer, Halloway, embedded in her own crew, and learns the seizure conspiracy goes higher than her family—judges, land barons—who will kill to keep the deed buried. Voss must decide whose side she's truly on. Emotional beat: betrayal turned to resolve.

chapters.title: Race Above the Clouds
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. With the pass closing within hours, Rafael leads a skeleton crew up the final ascent through driving snow, laying rail across a viaduct above the clouds while Halloway's men shadow them. Emotional beat: exhilaration and terror fused—the best engineering of her life under worst conditions.

chapters.title: The Buried Cache
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. At the summit cutting, Rafael finds the cache in the gorge wall: Tomas's remains, his father's letters, and the original deed proving the provision lands were stolen. Halloway arrives with guns. Emotional beat: everything she came for, held at gunpoint.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. In the storm, the crew turns on Halloway together—Okoye's blasting, Baptiste's strength, Nell's quick thinking, even Voss's testimony against her own family's fixers. Halloway is driven off the mountain empty-handed. Emotional beat: collective courage; the law failed them, so they don't fail each other.

chapters.title: Closing the Line
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Instead of completing the railroad that would open the stolen lands to the companies, Rafael fires the charges herself, collapsing the pass permanently. The deed survives—in copies sent to newspapers, courts, and Tomas's grave. Emotional beat: sacrifice; burning the bridge between her past and any easy future.

chapters.title: Years, Not Miles
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Spring. Rafael stands trial briefly, is cleared by the resurfaced evidence, and declines every offer to rebuild railroads. She plants a garden on the provision land returned to the families, visits Tomas's cairn, and stays put for a whole year. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—she has stopped measuring life in miles and begun living in years.
